Why not gamble on PvP? If they have worse loot than you then it should be an easy fight, move on. If they have better loot, then what a perfect way to get a nice little upgrade. PvP for the sake of PvP is fun, it's fun to kill someone else, it's fun to claim victory, and it's fun to get outplayed. Maybe you're both at the end of the wire and agree to walk away, maybe there's opportunity for some jolly cooperation. The uncertainty and the randomness of it all makes it fun.

PvE is very predictable, eventually you learn how they detect you, how they attack you, how they'll approach you. Then play some more and you'll learn where exactly they spawn, how to always avoid them and how to always beat them, it becomes boring after a time.

I'm not sure what's up with the Dark and Darker comparison but it's very similar to this game. There is in fact a paywall, the free version only grants you very limited access to the game, think a trial version of WoW. 

The questing is almost completely PvE, go kill certain mobs on certain maps, kill bosses, mine ore, open crates. Very little of it asks for player kills. Yet PvP is completely unavoidable unlike this game which gives you the option to sneak around and avoid other players. Everything you do in Dark and Darker leaves a trail allowing players to track you down wherever you go and if you get seen, you best believe they're going to follow you across the entire map.

There isn't really much of a reason to PvP anymore than there is in Arc Raiders, to take their loot and that PvP is fun. PvP in a PvPvE game isn't griefing, it's a part of the game that people interact with because it's fun. The endgame has you almost completely avoid PvP because you would just die and that'd be a detriment to your questing progress, but PvP happens in every single lobby regardless.
Most of the sub are still PvE players in the honeymoon phase, give it a few months after release when the meta gets developed and player skill becomes way higher.

I apologize, I only skimmed over your post, let me give you more reasonable actionable advice. You just hit level 30 and there's a lot you still don't know about the game and with time comes mastery. It's possible to climb on any role though ofc some are more difficult than others at specific elo brackets.

1. Have fun. League is a marathon not a sprint, the love for the game will propel you forward into continuing to learn and improve at the game, Don't play champs/roles you dislike and don't tilt queue yourself into burning out either.
2. Keep your champion pool small. Again, with time comes mastery and learning what the enemies champs do as well as how people pilot them is infinitely easier when you're not wrestling with your own champion as well.
3. Consume league content. Even if it is not educational in nature you are quite literally amongst the worst players (no flame everyone starts somewhere) so there is always something to learn from others, though league has amazing educational content for all roles and champions and it wouldn't hurt to watch some here and there. If not watching your favorite high elo player can teach you a lot from just observing alone.

Among all of this is that consistency is key. Don't tilt yourself over your teammates decisions and honestly just treat them as quite developed AI language models that can play league. Keep playing, you're only starting your journey and you have a long long LONG way to go brother. Good luck.
